title: Count CI-reused passing checks as commands run in the verdict
summary: When the checks stage reused a green CI run for the candidate commit, judge() in verify.rs should count those passing records as seen commands, so a behavior criterion citing cargo fmt, clippy or test is met. Goal: stop rejecting passing jobs; audience is the verdict and whoever reads its criteria results. Reused records get an explicit CheckRun field, with old records still loading.

defaults_applied.how: New unit tests in verify.rs and records.rs.
Fix in judge()'s seen-command rule, not by loosening the criterion check.
Criteria run judge() on reused-check inputs.
The outcome is a passing job no longer rejected for unseen commands.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Code survey: read crates/athena-core/src/verify.rs (judge() at ~line 308 builds `ran` from commands_run, then adds passing records only when `candidate_tree == checks_tree` and `exit_code == Some(0)`; a reused CI record has no exit code, so it never counts), crates/athena-core/src/checks.rs (~line 230-254 builds reused records from a CiRecord with note 'result reused from the ... for {sha}'; that is the producer to mark), crates/athena-core/src/routing.rs (~267 runs_from_record, resolves reuse before local runs) and crates/athena-data/src/records.rs (CheckRun at ~751, `deny_unknown_fields`, existing optional fields use `#[serde(default, skip_serializing_if)]`). Records validation: `check_record_file` (records.rs ~2927) parses into `AnyRecord` (~2613), so a new `#[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "...")] reused: bool` on CheckRun is accepted by deny_unknown_fields; old records without it load via default. The existing round-trip test `failing_test_names_round_trip_and_are_read_per_check` (records.rs ~4227) and the CheckRun literal at ~4188 are the pattern for covering it; the producer adds a similar old-record-still-loads test. Behavior is measured directly by calling judge() on VerdictInputs in verify.rs unit tests (existing helper judge_recorded ~816), not through a stand-in.

Commit match: the record counts only when it is for the candidate commit. CheckRun has no commit field, so the producer decides how judge() knows the commit (for example the existing checks_tree/candidate_tree equality, or a recorded sha next to the reused flag); the test must show a different-commit record stays unmet.
No governance file (athena.toml, defaults.toml, workflows) needs to change.

acceptance_criteria.text: A new unit test in crates/athena-core/src/verify.rs builds VerdictInputs with passing checks reused from CI (exit_code None, reused field set, same tree and commit) and a behavior criterion citing `cargo test`, and asserts the criterion is met with commands_verified true. Run `cargo test -p athena-core verify`; the test passes, and it fails on the base code (judge() ignores records without exit code 0).

Unit tests in verify.rs show a reused record for a different commit/tree, a failed reused record, and a skipped record each leave the `cargo test` behavior criterion unmet. Run `cargo test -p athena-core verify`.

CheckRun in crates/athena-data/src/records.rs gains a serde-defaulted boolean field marking reused records (not note-text matching), crates/athena-core/src/checks.rs sets it where reused records are built, and judge() reads the field, not the note string (Grep for the note text in verify.rs finds no matching on it).

A records.rs test deserializes a CheckRun JSON without the new field and it loads with the field false, and a reused record round-trips through check_record_file/AnyRecord. Run `cargo test -p athena-data`.
CHANGELOG.md has an entry describing that checks reused from a green CI run for the candidate commit now count as commands run in the verdict (D43, D115).

out_of_scope: Changing how or when CI results are fetched or reused
Changing the baseline or pre-existing failure logic
Listing a repository-wide fmt, clippy or test run as its own acceptance criterion (the checks stage covers it)
urgent_reason: It stops passing jobs being wrongly rejected, which cuts failed attempts and redo-work retries.
hard_reason: This changes the verdict rule in judge() that decides whether a job's criteria are met and whether a job is rejected.
